comments: `_direct_state_changed() `should receive a `PhysicsDirectBodyState` object, not a `BoxShape` one. As the argument is not what expected, it's casted into a null object, making Godot to crash when trying to access it. Should the function just return and do nothing if the argument is not of type `PhysicsDirectBodyState`?

Function should in most situations return default value(e.g 0, false, empty Array etc.) and print error.
This is done(usually) by one of `ERR_FAIL` macros

The real question is: why is this method exposed? It's used internally by the physics engine to trigger an update in the scene. It's a hidden method, so not something that would normally be called, but I can't think of a reason that a user would want to call this method.

> The real question is: why is this method exposed? It's used internally by the physics engine to trigger an update in the scene. It's a hidden method, so not something that would normally be called, but I can't think of a reason that a user would want to call this method.

It's because it's used as a callback that goes through the method bindings:
```
scene/3d/physics_body.cpp
1076:   PhysicsServer::get_singleton()->body_set_force_integration_callback(get_rid(), this, "_direct_state_changed");
```

In `master` this can maybe be changed to use `callable_mp` so that the callback uses a function pointer, but in `3.x` that's not possible. So we have a number of internal methods exposed publicly because they're used as callbacks by engine internals (see https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/2285 which discusses it in reaction to this type of issue).

Looks that in 3.x branch there is for now 671 methods which starts with `_`(`_ready` etc. are also counted)
List of all functions - https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/2285#issuecomment-810005190

review_comments: It's now probably not needed, but it may still be worth keeping. However, if we are going to keep it, this check should be applied consistently in all the `_direct_state_changed()` methods. Also, a better error check for a `nullptr` is `ERR_FAIL_NULL_MSG`.

This should let you remove the `ClassDB::bind_method(D_METHOD("_body_moved"), &TestPhysics2DMainLoop::_body_moved);` which was only used for this callback.

(And maybe clear the two commented lines below this which won't be reused as is.)
You can also remove `ClassDB::bind_method("body_changed_transform", &TestPhysics3DMainLoop::body_changed_transform);` (and the whole `_bind_method` override).
